How much are these shoes? — They're 30,000 won.

explain_en: Shoes come as a pair, so you count them 한 켤레, 두 켤레. The verb for wearing them is 신다.

examples.en: My room is on the first floor.
It's in front of Exit 1.
Today is the first.
It's one minute to the subway station.
One plus two is three.

explain: 일은 숫자 1이에요. “work”도 “일”이고 “day”(날짜)도 “일”이에요. 소리가 같아서 문장을 보고 알아요.

phrases.example: 자전거로 출근하면 운동도 되고 돈도 아껴서 일석이조예요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 가지 일로 두 가지 좋은 것을 얻음
phrases.nuance_en: getting two good results from one action, like killing two birds with one stone

explain_en: 일 is the number 1. 일 also means “work” and “day of the month”. They sound the same, so you tell them apart from the sentence.

examples.en: My number is 010-2345-6789.
Bulgogi for two, please.
The bread is 2,000 won.
There is a cafe on the second floor.
Bus number 2 goes to City Hall.

explain: 숫자 2도 “이”이고 “this”도 “이”예요. 이 층은 “2층”일 수도 있고 “이 층(this floor)”일 수도 있어요. 문장을 보고 알아요.

phrases.example: 저녁 먹고 이 차로 노래방에 가요.
phrases.en: the second round (of a gathering, at a new place)
phrases.nuance_ko: 회식이나 모임에서 자리를 옮긴 두 번째 장소(보통 ‘2차’로 써요)
phrases.nuance_en: the second place a group moves to after dinner or a gathering, usually written ‘2차’
phrases.en_equiv: the second round (of a gathering, at a new place)

explain_en: The number 2 is 이, and so is “this”. 이 층 can mean “second floor” or “this floor”. The sentence tells you which.

examples.en: The classroom is on the 3rd floor.
It takes three minutes to get to school.
March is spring.

examples.ko: 삼 번 버스를 학교 앞에서 타요.
examples.en: I take bus number 3 in front of the school.
Three plus four is seven.

explain: 숫자 3은 한자어로 “삼”, 고유어로 “셋”이에요. 층, 번호, 돈, 분에는 “삼”을 써요.

explain_en: The number 3 is 삼 in Sino-Korean and 셋 in native Korean. Use 삼 for floors, numbers, money and minutes.

examples.en: This building has no 4th floor.
It's in front of Exit 4.
There are lots of flowers in April.
Four plus five is nine.
I wait four minutes for the bus.

explain: 사는 “죽음”을 뜻하는 한자와 소리가 같아서 조금 불길한 숫자예요. 그래서 4층을 “F”로 쓰는 건물이 많아요.

explain_en: 사 sounds like the word for “death”, so it is seen as unlucky. Many buildings label the 4th floor “F”.

examples.en: Just wait five minutes.

Five plus six is eleven.
I take Line 5.

explain: 5월 5일은 어린이날이에요. 한국에서는 쉬는 날이고, 아이들에게 선물을 줘요.
